description:
## Finding

At pinned origin/main `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`, `.agent/docs/telemetry.md:328-335` says drain-arbiter readiness movement wakes nothing because current product waits are polled and no scheduler waiter exists.

That statement is too broad. A scratch reachability probe on `compiler2::port_macros_test::item_macro_compiler_ast_splices_callable_fn` recorded:

```text
producer_pokes=0, unresolved=1, quiescence_steps=1
```

Deleting only the drive-loop `if quiescence_woke_work { continue; }` branch and helper made the same test fail immediately with:

```text
Unresolved {
  waits: [Settled(FunctionDefined(FunctionId(0)))],
  jobs: [SeedRoot(RootId(0))]
}
```

Product-pull waits are indeed polled rather than scheduler-subscribed, but agenda-level jobs such as `SeedRoot` can subscribe to settled facts and be woken by drain arbitration. fz-kdt.60 correctly retained this branch.

## Work

Update telemetry/fact-engine documentation to distinguish product-driver polling from agenda-level scheduler waiters. Add or strengthen a focused regression that exposes the SeedRoot settled waiter and proves the quiescence wake continues the drive.

## Acceptance

- Documentation no longer claims drain arbitration wakes nothing categorically.
- It states which product waits are polled and which agenda-level settled waiters remain scheduler-subscribed.
- A focused regression fails if the live drive-loop arbiter branch/helper is removed.
- Existing drain-arbiter telemetry tests, full library tests, formatting, and strict clippy pass.
title: Correct telemetry docs: drain arbitration wakes agenda-level SeedRoot settled waiters
